content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe the general structure of carbohydrates
Classify carbohydrates as monosaccharides, disaccharides, or polysaccharides
Explain the functions of different carbohydrates
Give examples of each type of carbohydrate

are molecules containing carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen. The hydrogen and oxygen are usually in a 2:1 ratio (like water). Carbohydrates include sugars and starches and serve as the main source of energy for most organisms.
Where n = number of carbon atoms
Can be used directly in respiration
α-glucose: -OH on carbon 1 below the ring
β-glucose: -OH on carbon 1 above the ring
Can be broken down when needed
Polysaccharides like starch are not sweet
Glucose and fructose are the same
Different sugars have different properties and functions
Molecule containing C, H, O with H:O ratio of 2:1
Carbohydrates contain C, H, O in ratio
Disaccharides: two sugars joined (sucrose, maltose, lactose)
Polysaccharides: many sugars joined (starch, glycogen, cellulose)
Glycosidic bonds join sugars via condensation
Functions include energy, storage, and structure
Polysaccharides are insoluble - good for storage
